chunks: 1 - The venerable Shaykh Abu Ja'far Muhammad ibn Ali ibn al-Husayn ibn Musa ibn Babawayh al-Qummi (may Allah have mercy on him) narrated to us. He said: Muhammad ibn Ibrahim ibn Ahmad al-Mu'adhi narrated to us. He said: Muhammad ibn al-Husayn narrated to us. He said: Abu al-Hasan Ali ibn Muhammad ibn Ali narrated to us. He said: Al-Hasan ibn Muhammad al-Marwazi narrated to us, from his father, from Yahya ibn Ayyash. He said: Ali ibn Asim al-Wasiti narrated to us. He said: Ata' ibn al-Sa'ib informed me, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, from Ibn Abbas, who said: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said, while his companions were discussing the virtues of Sha'ban in his presence:

and his companions were discussing the virtues of Sha'ban in his presence. He said: It is a noble month, and it is my month. The carriers of the Throne magnify it and recognize its right. It is a month in which the sustenance of the believers is increased, like the month of Ramadan. In it, Paradise is adorned. It was named Sha'ban because the sustenance of the believers branches out therein. It is a month in which deeds are multiplied: a good deed is rewarded seventyfold, evil deeds are erased, sins are forgiven, good deeds are accepted, and the Almighty -- glory be to His majesty -- boasts about His worshippers therein. He looks upon those who fast and those who stand in prayer, and He boasts about them to the carriers of the Throne.

Then Ali ibn Abi Talib (peace be upon him) stood and said: May my father and mother be sacrificed for you, O Messenger of Allah! Describe for us some of its virtues so that we may increase in our desire to fast and stand in prayer during it, and so that we may strive for the Majestic, the Mighty, the Glorious, therein. The Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) said:

Whoever fasts the first day of Sha'ban, Allah will record seventy good deeds for him, each good deed being equivalent to one year of worship. Whoever fasts two days of Sha'ban, the ruinous sin will be erased from him. Whoever fasts three days of Sha'ban will be raised by seventy levels in Paradise of pearls and rubies. Whoever fasts four days of Sha'ban, his sustenance will be expanded for him. Whoever fasts five days of Sha'ban will be made beloved among the servants. Whoever fasts six days of Sha'ban will be spared from seventy types of calamity. Whoever fasts seven days of Sha'ban will be protected from Iblis and his soldiers for his lifetime. Whoever fasts eight days of Sha'ban will not depart this world until he is given to drink from the holy ponds. Whoever fasts nine days of Sha'ban, Munkar and Nakir will show him gentleness when they question him. Whoever fasts ten days of Sha'ban, Allah will expand his grave by seventy arm-lengths. Whoever fasts eleven days of Sha'ban will have eleven towers of light erected upon his grave. Whoever fasts twelve days of Sha'ban, ninety thousand angels will visit him in his grave every day until the Trumpet is blown. Whoever fasts thirteen days of Sha'ban, the angels of the seven heavens will seek forgiveness for him. Whoever fasts fourteen days of Sha'ban, animals, beasts, and even whales in the seas will be inspired to seek forgiveness for him. Whoever fasts fifteen days of Sha'ban, the Lord of Glory will call out: By My might and My majesty, I will not burn you in the Fire. Whoever fasts sixteen days of Sha'ban, seventy seas of fire will be extinguished from him. Whoever fasts seventeen days of Sha'ban, all the gates of Hell will be locked from him. Whoever fasts eighteen days of Sha'ban, all the gates of Paradise will be opened for him. Whoever fasts nineteen days of Sha'ban will be given seventy thousand palaces of pearl and ruby in Paradise. Whoever fasts twenty days of Sha'ban will be wed to seventy thousand houris. Whoever fasts twenty-one days of Sha'ban, the angels will welcome him and wipe him with their wings. Whoever fasts twenty-two days of Sha'ban will be clothed with seventy thousand robes of fine silk and brocade. Whoever fasts twenty-three days of Sha'ban will be brought a creature of light when he comes out of his grave, upon which he will fly to Paradise. Whoever fasts twenty-four days of Sha'ban will intercede for seventy thousand people of monotheism. Whoever fasts twenty-five days of Sha'ban will be given immunity from hypocrisy. Whoever fasts twenty-six days of Sha'ban, Allah the Mighty and Majestic will write for him a permit upon the Path. Whoever fasts twenty-seven days of Sha'ban, Allah will write for him immunity from the Fire. Whoever fasts twenty-eight days of Sha'ban, his face will shine radiantly on the Day of Resurrection. Whoever fasts twenty-nine days of Sha'ban will attain the greatest pleasure of Allah. Whoever fasts thirty days of Sha'ban, Gabriel will call to him from before the Throne: O you! Begin your deeds anew, for what has passed and preceded of your sins has been forgiven. The Majestic, Mighty and Majestic, says: Even if your sins were equal to the number of stars of the sky, the drops of rain, the leaves of trees, the grains of sand and soil, and the days of this world, I would forgive them for you — and that is not difficult for Allah after your fasting of the month of Sha'ban.
Ibn Abbas said: This is for the month of Sha'ban.

key_terms.الحور العين: Houris, the companions of Paradise described in the Quran
key_terms.الصراط: The Bridge (Sirat), the bridge over Hell that all must cross on Judgment Day
key_terms.حملة العرش: Carriers of the Throne, the angels who bear God's Throne
key_terms.شعبان: Sha'ban, the eighth month of the Islamic calendar, preceding Ramadan
key_terms.منكر ونكير: Munkar and Nakir, the two angels who question the dead in the grave

ai.seo_question: What are the rewards for fasting each day of Sha'ban according to the Prophet Muhammad?
ai.summary: This lengthy hadith, narrated through Ibn Abbas, records the Prophet Muhammad (SAWW) enumerating the spiritual rewards for fasting each successive day of the month of Sha'ban, from the first day through all thirty days, with escalating benefits. The Prophet was prompted by Imam Ali (AS) who asked him to describe Sha'ban's virtues in detail. Historically, this teaching was given during a gathering where the companions were discussing the merits of Sha'ban, reflecting the early Muslim community's practice of seeking detailed knowledge about acts of worship and their rewards.
